title: HTML5 & Semantic Structure
summary: HTML5 document structure, semantic tags (<header>, <main>, <nav>, <article>, <aside>, <footer>), and DOM accessibility fundamentals.

explanation.overview: Semantic HTML means using HTML elements according to their intended structural purpose. Rather than relying on generic <div> containers, semantic tags convey meaning to both the browser, search engines, and screen readers.

sections.heading: Core Semantic Landmark Tags
sections.content: HTML5 introduces structural landmark tags that organize the document outline cleanly.
bulletPoints: <header>: Introductory content, site branding, and primary navigation.
<nav>: Section containing major site navigation links.
<main>: Primary unique content block of the document (should only appear once per page).
<article>: Self-contained independent content piece suitable for syndication (e.g., blog post, comment).
<section>: Thematic grouping of content, typically with a heading.
<footer>: Document or section footer containing copyright, contact, or related links.

sections.heading: Benefits for SEO & Accessibility
sections.content: Screen readers utilize semantic landmarks to allow visually impaired users to jump directly to main content or navigation. Search engine crawlers prioritize semantic elements to weigh content hierarchy.
bulletPoints: Improves accessibility (WCAG compliance) out of the box.
Enhances search engine indexability and rich snippets.
Simplifies CSS styling and code maintainability.

keyTakeaways: Always use landmark elements (<main>, <nav>, <header>) instead of generic <div> tags.
Ensure one unique <main> element exists per page.
Semantic HTML enhances screen reader accessibility and search engine ranking.

title: HTML Forms & ARIA Accessibility
summary: Form controls, label associations, validation attributes, and WAI-ARIA attributes for accessible web interfaces.

explanation.overview: HTML forms are the core interactive mechanism on the web. Accessible forms associate explicit labels with inputs, specify semantic input types, and use ARIA attributes when native HTML elements fall short.

sections.heading: Form Labeling & Native Validation
sections.content: Every interactive input must be explicitly associated with a <label> element using matching for and id attributes.
bulletPoints: Explicit Association: <label for="email">Email</label><input id="email" type="email" />.
Native Types: type="email", type="number", type="url", type="date" enable mobile-optimized keyboards.
Attributes: required, minlength, maxlength, pattern allow browser-level validation before submission.

sections.heading: WAI-ARIA Essentials
sections.content: WAI-ARIA (Web Accessibility Initiative - Accessible Rich Internet Applications) defines attributes to complement custom UI controls.
bulletPoints: aria-label: Supplies text label when no visible text exists.
aria-expanded: Indicates open/closed state of dropdowns or accordions.
aria-live: Announces dynamic asynchronous DOM updates to screen readers.

keyTakeaways: Always connect <label for="..."> with <input id="...">.
Use native HTML input types for built-in mobile keyboards and validation.
Use ARIA attributes to describe dynamic states to assistive technologies.

mcqs.question: Which ARIA attribute communicates the open or collapsed state of an accordion toggle?
mcqs.explanation: aria-expanded="true|false" informs screen readers whether an interactive region is open or closed.

title: CSS Box Model & Specificity
summary: Content, padding, border, margin layout mechanics, box-sizing: border-box, and CSS rule specificity calculation.

explanation.overview: Every element rendered in CSS is formatted as a rectangular box. The CSS Box Model consists of content, padding, border, and margin. Understanding box-sizing and selector specificity is crucial to building accurate web layouts.

sections.heading: Box Model Architecture
sections.content: An element's rendered size depends on how box-sizing is declared.
bulletPoints: content-box (default): Total Width = width + left/right padding + left/right border.
border-box (recommended): Total Width = width (padding and border are absorbed inside).

sections.heading: Selector Specificity Formula
sections.content: CSS specificity resolves cascade conflicts when multiple rules target the same element.
bulletPoints: Inline Styles: (1,0,0,0) - e.g. style="color: red".
IDs: (0,1,0,0) - e.g. #header.
Classes, Pseudo-classes, Attributes: (0,0,1,0) - e.g. .btn, :hover, [type="text"].
Elements & Pseudo-elements: (0,0,0,1) - e.g. div, p, ::before.

keyTakeaways: Set `box-sizing: border-box` globally (`* { box-sizing: border-box; }`) for predictable layout sizing.
Margin collapses vertically between adjacent block elements.
IDs outweigh classes; classes outweigh element selectors in CSS specificity.

codeExamples.description: Standard CSS box-sizing reset applied across all elements.

mcqs.question: With `box-sizing: border-box`, what is the total rendered width of a div with `width: 200px`, `padding: 20px`, `border: 5px`?
mcqs.explanation: With border-box, padding and border are included inside the specified 200px width.

mcqs.question: Which CSS selector has the highest specificity score?
mcqs.explanation: An ID selector (#sidebar) has specificity (0,1,0,0), outranking classes and element selectors.

title: CSS Flexbox & CSS Grid
summary: 1D layout distribution with Flexbox vs 2D structural layout system with CSS Grid.

explanation.overview: Modern CSS relies on Flexbox for 1-dimensional layouts (components, toolbars, alignment) and CSS Grid for 2-dimensional overall page grids (rows and columns simultaneously).

sections.heading: CSS Flexbox (1D Layout)
sections.content: Flexbox distributes space along a main-axis and cross-axis.
bulletPoints: flex-direction: row | column defines main axis.
justify-content: flex-start | center | space-between aligns along main axis.
align-items: center | stretch | flex-end aligns along cross axis.
gap: Defines space between flex items.

sections.heading: CSS Grid (2D Layout)
sections.content: Grid creates explicit rows and columns for complete layout control.
bulletPoints: grid-template-columns: repeat(12, 1fr) creates fluid column tracks.
grid-template-areas: Defines named layout regions visually.
auto-fit / auto-fill with minmax(): Builds responsive card grids without media queries.

keyTakeaways: Use Flexbox for 1D component alignment (headers, button groups, nav bars).
Use CSS Grid for 2D page layouts and multi-column grid cards.
Combine `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(250px, 1fr))` for media-query-free responsive grids.

codeExamples.title: Responsive Card Grid
codeExamples.description: Media-query-free responsive grid with auto-fit and minmax.

mcqs.question: Which property aligns flex items along the CROSS axis in Flexbox?
mcqs.explanation: align-items aligns items perpendicular to the main flex axis.

mcqs.question: What is the primary difference between CSS Flexbox and CSS Grid?
options: Flexbox is 1D (rows OR columns); Grid is 2D (rows AND columns)
Flexbox only works on mobile devices
Flexbox requires JavaScript to calculate positions
mcqs.explanation: Flexbox manages 1-dimensional positioning; Grid handles 2-dimensional rows and columns together.

title: Responsive Web Design & Media Queries
summary: Mobile-first CSS strategy, viewport meta tag, breakpoints, fluid typography, and CSS custom properties.

explanation.overview: Responsive Web Design (RWD) ensures web applications look and perform seamlessly across mobile screens, tablets, laptops, and 4K desktop displays.

sections.heading: Mobile-First Methodology
sections.content: Write default CSS styles targeting mobile screens first, then layer on min-width media queries for larger displays.
bulletPoints: Viewport Meta Tag: <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0"> is required.
min-width Media Queries: @media (min-width: 768px) { ... } for tablet/desktop overrides.
Fluid Units: rem, em, %, vw, vh, and clamp(min, val, max) for scalable typography.

sections.heading: CSS Variables (Custom Properties)
sections.content: Declare scoped design tokens that adapt dynamically within media queries or dark-mode themes.
bulletPoints: Declaration: --bg-primary: #0a0a0a;.
Usage: background-color: var(--bg-primary);.
Theme switching: Easily override variables under .dark class.

keyTakeaways: Always include the viewport meta tag in your HTML <head>.
Build mobile-first CSS using `min-width` media query breakpoints.
Use CSS custom properties (`var(--var-name)`) for responsive theme tokens.

codeExamples.title: Mobile-First Media Query & CSS Variables
codeExamples.description: Responsive layout using min-width breakpoints and CSS variables.

mcqs.question: In a mobile-first CSS architecture, which type of media query is primarily used?
mcqs.explanation: Mobile-first applies base styles for small screens, using min-width to enhance layout on larger displays.

mcqs.question: What is the purpose of `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">`?
options: To instruct mobile browsers to render the layout at device screen width without auto-zooming out
mcqs.explanation: The viewport meta tag matches page width to screen width, establishing mobile scale.
